Here’s a quick, reusable recipe you can drop into your own script or notebook.  
It shows how to hit a typical “list‑files” endpoint, filter by domain, and pull out just the identifiers (plus any extra fields you care about).

```python
import requests

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1️⃣  Configuration – put your real values here
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
API_BASE_URL   = "https://api.example.com/v1"          # ← change to your provider’s base URL
ENDPOINT       = "/files"                              # ← the path that returns file metadata
API_KEY        = "dload_key"                           # ← your secret key
DOMAIN_FILTER  = "downloads.com"                       # ← the domain you’re interested in
HEADERS        = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣  Build the request
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
params = {
    "filter[domain]": DOMAIN_FILTER,   # many APIs support a query‑string filter
    "page[size]": 1000,                # adjust pagination size as needed
    # add more params if you want to narrow the result set further
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣  Make the HTTP call
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
response = requests.get(f"{API_BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", headers=HEADERS, params=params)
response.raise_for_status()            # will raise an exception on non‑200 status codes

data = response.json()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4️⃣  Pull out what you need
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
file_ids = [item["id"] for item in data["items"]]          # <-- list of IDs
# If you also want other context attributes:
extra_attrs = [
    {
        "id": item["id"],
        "name": item.get("name"),
        "size_bytes": item.get("size"),
        "downloaded_at": item.get("created_at")
    }
    for item in data["items"]
]

print("IDs:", file_ids)
print("Context snapshot:", extra_attrs[:5])   # show first 5 for brevity
```

### What this does

| Step | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **Configuration** | Set the base URL, endpoint, and auth header. |
| **Params** | Pass a `filter[domain]` query parameter (or whatever your API uses) so the server only returns files from *downloads.com*. |
| **Request** | Send a GET request with the proper headers and parameters. |
| **Parse** | Convert the JSON payload into a Python dict. |
| **Extract** | Build a simple list of IDs (`file_ids`) and optionally a richer list of dictionaries containing any other fields you want (`extra_attrs`). |

> **Tip:** If the API paginates results, loop over pages until you’ve collected all items. Most services expose a `next_page_url` or similar field in the response.

Feel free to adapt the field names (`"items"`, `"id"`, `"name"`, etc.) to match the exact shape of your provider’s JSON schema.
